title: Ouch! Bear Cub Gets a Paw Full of Porcupine Quills
summary:
Imagine touching a cactus and getting dozens of tiny needles stuck in your hand. That's what happened to a young bear cub in Alaska! The cub, named 901jr, was spotted on a live webcam with a paw covered in spiky porcupine quills. Porcupines have about 30,000 sharp quills to protect themselves. Even though brown bears are big and strong, a curious cub can get a painful surprise.

Cub 901jr lives in Katmai National Park, a place famous for its huge brown bears. Every summer, the bears gather at Brooks Falls to catch salmon swimming upstream. The live bear cam lets people watch them fish, play, and sometimes get into trouble. This cub's mom is a bear named 901. She has blond-tipped ears and golden-brown fur. Earlier this summer, she was seen with two cubs, but sadly one died. This year, some mother bears have even killed cubs, which is very rare and sad.

Porcupine quills are like tiny spears with barbs on the end. They can be painful but usually fall out on their own. The cub will probably be fine. As it grows, it will learn to stay away from prickly animals. You can watch the bears live online and maybe even vote for the fattest one in Fat Bear Week!
why_it_matters: This reminds us that even strong animals can get hurt when they ignore nature's warning signs — just like you learn to be careful around things that poke, sting, or bite.

background_read: Katmai National Park (a protected wild area in southern Alaska) is one of the best places in the world to watch brown bears in their natural home.
Porcupines cannot shoot their quills, but the quills detach easily when another animal touches them.
Fat Bear Week is a real online tournament where fans choose the fattest bear as a fun way to celebrate the bears.
Article_Structure: WHO: A young brown bear cub named 901jr and its mother, a bear named 901.
WHAT: The cub was spotted on a live webcam with a paw covered in spiky porcupine quills.
WHERE: Katmai National Park, near Brooks Falls, where brown bears gather to catch salmon.
WHY: The curious cub probably got too close to a porcupine, whose sharp quills are used for protection.

perspectives.description: They feel sorry for the cub with quills in its paw and hope it is not in too much pain.
They stay calm because porcupine quills usually fall out on their own, and young cubs learn from such mistakes.
They enjoy watching the bears on the live cam and see Fat Bear Week as a fun way to connect with wild animals.
